findings.title: Raw HTML imports bypass sanitization and allow stored XSS
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` stores external feed/article content with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders `post.cooked` with `raw`, so Discourse's normal HTML sanitizer is completely bypassed. `PollFeed` also calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, which can turn escaped `<script>` into an active `<script>` before import. Anyone controlling or compromising the configured feed/article can execute JavaScript in the Discourse origin (and inside the embed iframe). Sanitize imported HTML with the existing allowed-tag/attribute sanitizer before saving, or do not use raw_html for untrusted feed content.

findings.title: Imported-from footer interpolates an untrusted URL into raw HTML
findings.body: `url` comes from an RSS/Atom item and is only checked with a loose `^https?://` regex. It is interpolated directly into `href='#{url}'` and appended to the raw HTML body. A URL containing a single quote and attribute text, such as `http://host/'onmouseover='alert(1)`, can produce an extra event-handler attribute in the generated anchor. Because the post is stored as raw HTML, this is another stored XSS vector. Escape the URL with `ERB::Util.html_escape` or build the link with `link_to` and sanitize the final HTML.

findings.title: Referer value is interpolated into JavaScript without escaping
findings.body: `request.referer` is a request header, and the only validation is that its host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Its path/query is interpolated unescaped into a JavaScript string. A referer such as `http://eviltrout.com/';alert(1);//` breaks out of the string and executes in the Discourse iframe, allowing script in the Discourse origin. Escape the value with `escape_javascript`/`to_json` and use a fixed or parsed origin for the `postMessage` target instead of the raw referer.

findings.title: Invalid `end if` makes the best view fail to compile
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` is not valid Ruby: it closes the `if` and then starts an `if` modifier with no condition. Rendering the `best` action after a topic has been found will raise a template syntax error, so existing embeds return 500 instead of displaying the topic. It should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: PostCreator is called inside an outer transaction, so jobs are enqueued before commit
findings.body: `PostCreator.create` is invoked inside `Topic.transaction`. `PostCreator` opens its own transaction but it nests inside this one, so its internal block does not commit before it calls `enqueue_jobs` (process_post, feature_topic_users, etc.). Those Sidekiq jobs may run before the topic/post are committed and fail to find them; if the subsequent `TopicEmbed.create!` fails, for example during a duplicate-URL race, the outer transaction rolls back the post/topic but the already-enqueued jobs remain. Use after_commit callbacks or avoid wrapping PostCreator in an outer transaction.

findings.title: Embed endpoint enqueues retrieval jobs for arbitrary embed URLs
findings.body: `best` only checks the request's Referer host; it never checks that `params[:embed_url]` is on the embeddable host before enqueuing `retrieve_topic`. Any non-browser client can forge `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/` and send unlimited distinct `embed_url`s. The host is rejected later inside `TopicRetriever`, after the Sidekiq job has been accepted, and `invalid_host?` short-circuits before the Redis throttle, so invalid URLs are never throttled. This allows unauthenticated queue flooding, and the loading page reloads every 30 seconds, enqueueing more jobs. Validate the embed URL host and throttle before enqueueing.

findings.title: PollFeed tests for feed URL and username do not enable polling
findings.body: In the 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples, `feed_polling_enabled?` is left at its default `false`. The `&&` chain stops at that first condition, so `poll_feed` is never called regardless of the URL or username setting, and these tests still pass even if those checks are removed. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true, along with the other required settings, in those examples.

findings.title: Disqus import now depends on remote fetches and drops the category option
findings.body: The import task now creates the initial post through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which fetches `t[:link]` over the network and returns nil if the fetch fails or the link is not an HTTP URL. In that case the entire thread's comments are skipped, whereas the old code always created a topic from the local XML. The `--category` option was also removed, so existing invocations using it fail and imported threads no longer receive the requested category. Keep a fallback initial post/category or handle the failure explicitly.
